interview.q: What three values does a border shorthand need at minimum?
interview.answer: Width, style and colour; omitting style makes the border invisible even if width and colour are set.

interview.q: What is the default border-style?
interview.answer: none, which is why no border appears until you set a style such as solid.

interview.q: What does border: 0 do differently from border: none?
interview.answer: Both remove the border, but border: 0 also resets the width to zero, which matters for form controls.

interview.q: How do you round only the top corners of a box?
interview.answer: Use border-radius with two values, or the longhand border-top-left-radius and border-top-right-radius.

interview.q: What does a single value in border-radius do?
interview.answer: It sets the radius of all four corners equally.

interview.q: What does border-radius: 50% create?
interview.answer: A circle when the box is square, or an ellipse when the box is rectangular.

interview.q: What is the difference between border and outline for focus styles?
interview.answer: Border changes layout and box size; outline is drawn outside and does not affect layout, so it is safer for focus rings.

interview.q: Why is outline-offset useful?
interview.answer: It pushes the focus ring away from the element so it does not overlap content or get clipped.

interview.q: What does box-shadow accept?
interview.answer: Horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, spread radius and colour, plus an optional inset keyword.

interview.q: What does inset do in a box-shadow?
interview.answer: It draws the shadow inside the box instead of outside, useful for pressed or recessed effects.

interview.q: Why do multiple box-shadows not affect layout?
interview.answer: Shadows are paint effects only; they do not create boxes or change dimensions.

interview.q: How do you create a layered shadow?
interview.answer: Comma-separate multiple shadow declarations, with the first on top.

interview.q: What is the difference between blur and spread?
interview.answer: Blur softens the edge; spread grows or shrinks the shadow before blurring.

interview.q: What does a negative spread do?
interview.answer: It shrinks the shadow, which can create a sharp, smaller shadow behind the box.

interview.q: Why might a box shadow be clipped?
interview.answer: An ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it because the shadow paints outside the padding box.

interview.q: What is text-shadow?
interview.answer: A shadow applied to text glyphs, with offsets, blur and colour, similar to box-shadow but for text.

interview.q: Can text-shadow be layered?
interview.answer: Yes, comma-separate multiple shadows to create outlines or glow effects.

interview.q: What is the difference between border-color and outline-color?
interview.answer: border-color colours the border box; outline-color colours the outline, which sits outside the border.

interview.q: What does border-style: dashed do?
interview.answer: It draws a dashed line; the dash pattern is browser-defined and cannot be customised in standard CSS.

interview.q: What is border-image?
interview.answer: It slices an image into nine parts and stretches or repeats them to form a border.

interview.q: When is border-image useful?
interview.answer: For decorative frames or ornaments that cannot be achieved with solid colours.

interview.q: What does border-collapse do?
interview.answer: It merges adjacent borders in a table into a single border.

interview.q: What is the difference between separate and collapse border models?
interview.answer: Separate gives each cell its own border with spacing; collapse merges shared borders into one.

interview.q: What does border-spacing control?
interview.answer: The gap between cells in the separate border model.

interview.q: Why might focus outlines be removed and what should replace them?
interview.answer: Removing them hurts keyboard users; replace with a visible :focus-visible style instead of removing all focus styles.

interview.q: What is :focus-visible?
interview.answer: It matches when the browser decides a focus indicator should be shown, typically for keyboard navigation.

interview.q: Why is :focus-visible better than :focus for mouse users?
interview.answer: It avoids showing a focus ring on mouse clicks while keeping it for keyboard users.

interview.q: What does clip-path do to an element's visible shape?
interview.answer: It clips the element to a basic shape or polygon, hiding parts outside the path.

interview.q: Does clip-path affect layout?
interview.answer: No, the box keeps its original size; only the painted region is clipped.

interview.q: What is the difference between clip-path and mask?
interview.answer: clip-path uses a vector path; mask uses an image with alpha or luminance to control visibility.

interview.q: What does filter: drop-shadow do differently from box-shadow?
interview.answer: It follows the alpha shape of the element, so it shadows transparent parts and non-rectangular shapes correctly.

interview.q: Why use filter: drop-shadow on a PNG with transparency?
interview.answer: Because box-shadow would draw a rectangle around the image, while drop-shadow follows the visible pixels.

interview.q: What does border-radius do to a box-shadow?
interview.answer: The shadow follows the rounded corners of the box.

interview.q: What is a ridge or groove border?
interview.answer: A 3D-effect border style that looks raised or carved; rarely used in modern designs.

interview.q: What does outline-style: auto do?
interview.answer: It lets the browser choose a platform-native outline style, often used for focus indicators.

interview.q: Why might a border be invisible even with a width?
interview.answer: If border-style is none or the colour matches the background, nothing is painted.

interview.q: What is the difference between border and box-shadow for a line?
interview.answer: border is part of the box and affects size; box-shadow is paint-only and can create lines without layout changes.

interview.q: How do you create a one-pixel divider without a border?
interview.answer: Use a box-shadow with zero blur and a small spread, or a pseudo-element with a background.

interview.q: What does border-top-style: hidden do?
interview.answer: In the collapsing border model it suppresses the border; in the separate model it behaves like none.

interview.q: Why is border-radius preferred over images for rounded corners?
interview.answer: It scales, adapts to content and avoids extra HTTP requests.

interview.q: What is the effect of a large border-radius on a small box?
interview.answer: The corners overlap and the shape becomes a capsule or circle.

interview.q: How do you create a capsule shape?
interview.answer: Set border-radius to a value larger than half the height, such as 999px.

interview.q: What is the difference between border and outline for printing?
interview.answer: Both print, but outlines may be omitted by some browsers; borders are reliable.

interview.q: Why might box-shadow cause performance issues?
interview.answer: Large blurs on many elements force expensive paint operations, especially during scroll or animation.

interview.q: What does filter: blur do?
interview.answer: It blurs the element and its children, often used for backgrounds or modal backdrops.
